setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Phil opens the Dark Star, which this reviewer rates among the best ever; Dark Star sits in a Playin' sandwich with a bass solo and Feelin' Groovy jam leading into Morning Dew [7][14][17]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Bird Song features a raw, jamming performance that helps make the first set strong [16]
- **Loser** (1 review): Loser is played hot and helps the first set heat up [11]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw is a hot version that follows Loser in the first set [11]
- **El Paso** (1 other source): A 'Yellow Rose of Texas' tuning occurs just before El Paso [1]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Fast-paced band jamming with Billy giving a strong backdrop, then a short drum solo leads into Dark Star [7]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-10-18.139725.sbd.miller.sirmick.remaster.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 193 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Random ticks and crackles removed, Morning Dew distortion reduced, and a Jack Straw dropout repaired [1]
- **gd1972-10-18.132378.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 193 min; rated 3.43/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd72-10-18.sbd.weir.7295.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 168 min; rated 4.58/5 by 31 [4]. Said about its sound: Bobby is up in the mix at times; Rhythm guitar is too loud and Jerry's vocals are very low in the mix; Weir is mixed as loud as everyone else, so all his playing is audible [8][9][10][11][14][15][16]
- **gd1972-10-18.sbd.matera.123571.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 166 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Inherent distortion on the right channel made a pristine sound hard to achieve [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer, a Kansas University student, had tickets for the 17th and 19th but stayed in town to see every night [13]
- Met Bear backstage, who got him in early for this show with his pick of seats [13]
- Reviewer places this among the top five shows of 1972 [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-10-18.139725.sbd.miller.sirmick.remaster.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: SBD > Master Reel > Dat [1]. Also: Remaster of shnid 132378, with pitch correction from Mexicali Blues to the end of the show [1]
- **gd1972-10-18.132378.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat [2]. Also: The first three songs carry a cassette generation; this version upgrades away from it [2]
- **gd72-10-18.sbd.weir.7295.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Lineage is soundboard to master reel to cassette to DAT to CDR, with a disc 2 fix via Charles Weir [4]
- **gd1972-10-18.sbd.matera.123571.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Phil Matera; source: Unknown SBD source (probably shnid 7295) CD > wav > cool edit 2000 > flac [6]
